statement: Creatine monohydrate (3-5 g/day) combined with resistance training produces consistent additional gains in muscular strength and lean/regional muscle mass versus training alone; it amplifies training output and does not build muscle without the training stimulus.
effect_size: Small-to-moderate additive gains in strength and regional hypertrophy over resistance training alone; raises intramuscular phosphocreatine ~10-40%.
population: Healthy training adults across hundreds of RCTs (meta-analyses; Burke 2023 hypertrophy, Wang 2024 strength <50y)

provenance.primary: Burke et al., Nutrients 2023 (regional hypertrophy SR/meta); Wang et al., Nutrients 2024 (strength meta, adults <50)

confidence_notes: Strongest evidence base of any sports supplement. Monohydrate is the only form with this evidence; alternative forms are marketing. Effect requires the training stimulus. Grade: REAL.

statement: Creatine supplementation produces a small improvement in memory and cognitive function in healthy individuals, with the largest effects under metabolic stress (sleep deprivation, aging) and in people with low baseline stores (e.g. vegetarians); the effect in young, rested omnivores is small.
effect_size: Small, real improvement in memory/cognition; concentrated in older adults and stressed/sleep-deprived states; modest-to-null in young rested omnivores.
population: Healthy adults across RCTs (Avgerinos 2018 SR; Prokopidis 2023 memory meta)

provenance.primary: Avgerinos et al., Exp Gerontol 2018 (cognition SR); Prokopidis et al., Nutr Rev 2023 (memory meta-analysis)

confidence_notes: Real but smaller than the strength effect, and state-dependent (stress/aging/vegetarian). Not a general nootropic. Grade: REAL (context-dependent).

statement: Long-term creatine monohydrate supplementation at recommended doses is safe in healthy individuals, with no evidence of kidney damage; the 'creatine harms kidneys' belief derives from a confounded serum-creatinine reading, not from outcome data.
effect_size: No demonstrated renal or other harm in healthy populations over long-term use.
population: Healthy adults; ISSN position-stand evidence synthesis

provenance.primary: Kreider et al. — International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine, J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2017

confidence_notes: Canonical safety reference. People with pre-existing kidney disease should consult a clinician. Grade: REAL.

statement: Creatine supplementation during resistance training does NOT produce a meaningful increase in bone mineral density in older adults, despite early hopeful claims.
effect_size: No significant bone-mineral-density benefit over resistance training alone.
population: Older adults in resistance-training RCTs (brief meta-analysis)

provenance.primary: Forbes et al. — Creatine Supplementation During Resistance Training Does Not Lead to Greater Bone Mineral Density in Older Humans, Front Nutr 2018
provenance.surfaced_via: PubMed E-utilities (creatine bone older adults meta)

confidence_notes: Honest null logged alongside the positive creatine claims. The muscle/strength/cognition benefits stand; the bone claim does not.

statement: High-dose EPA/DHA (around 4 g/day) reliably lowers blood triglycerides ~20-30% in a dose-dependent manner and is endorsed by the American Heart Association as effective triglyceride-lowering therapy.
effect_size: ~20-30% triglyceride reduction at ~4 g/day EPA/DHA; dose-dependent.
population: Adults with elevated triglycerides across RCTs (AHA science advisory synthesis)

provenance.primary: Skulas-Ray et al. — Omega-3 Fatty Acids for the Management of Hypertriglyceridemia: AHA Science Advisory, Circulation 2019

confidence_notes: The cleanest real effect of fish oil. Distinct from cardiovascular-event reduction, which is equivocal. Grade: REAL (triglycerides).

statement: The omega-3 index (EPA+DHA as a percentage of red-cell fatty acids) is a risk predictor: low index tracks with higher cardiac death and worse inflammatory/mortality markers. This is a predictor, not proof that raising the index with supplements changes outcomes.
effect_size: Low omega-3 index (<4%) associates with higher cardiac-death risk vs high (>8%); low status associates with worse inflammatory and mortality biomarkers in large cohorts.
population: Cohort/biomarker studies (Harris & von Schacky 2004 concept; McBurney 2023 UK Biobank)

provenance.primary: Harris & von Schacky — The Omega-3 Index: a new risk factor for death from coronary heart disease?, Prev Med 2004; McBurney et al., Prostaglandins Leukot Essent Fatty Acids 2023 (UK Biobank)

confidence_notes: Honesty rule #1: predictor != lever. The index tracking with risk does not establish that supplementing to raise it improves outcomes. Grade: predictor (real), lever (unproven).

statement: Low-dose (1 g/day) marine omega-3 supplementation in the general population does not significantly reduce major cardiovascular events or cancer (VITAL); high-dose (4 g/day) prescription EPA (icosapent ethyl) reduced major cardiovascular events ~25% in high-triglyceride patients already on statins (REDUCE-IT), though the placebo choice is debated.
effect_size: VITAL: null primary CVD/cancer endpoints at 1 g/day. REDUCE-IT: ~25% relative reduction in major CV events at 4 g/day EPA in high-risk high-TG patients.
population: VITAL ~25,900 general-population adults; REDUCE-IT high-TG statin-treated high-risk patients

provenance.primary: Manson et al. — Marine n-3 Fatty Acids and Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease and Cancer (VITAL), NEJM 2019; Bhatt et al. — Icosapent Ethyl for Hypertriglyceridemia (REDUCE-IT), NEJM 2019

confidence_notes: REDUCE-IT secondary DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1812792. Net: OTC low-dose for primary prevention mostly null; high-dose Rx EPA in high-risk high-TG patients real. Grade: CONTEXT-ONLY (events).

statement: Vitamin D3 supplementation (2000 IU/day) does not reduce cancer incidence, major cardiovascular events, fractures, or progression to diabetes in generally-replete adult populations; the strong association between low vitamin D blood levels and disease largely reflects the level being a marker of poor health, not a causal lever.
effect_size: Null for cancer/CVD (VITAL), fractures (VITAL/LeBoff), and diabetes prevention (D2d non-significant trend) in replete populations.
population: VITAL ~25,900 adults; LeBoff fracture analysis; D2d ~2,400 prediabetic adults (4000 IU/day)

provenance.primary: Manson et al. — Vitamin D Supplements and Prevention of Cancer and CVD (VITAL), NEJM 2019; LeBoff et al. — Supplemental Vitamin D and Incident Fractures, NEJM 2022; Pittas et al. — Vitamin D and Prevention of Type 2 Diabetes (D2d), NEJM 2019
provenance.surfaced_via: PubMed E-utilities (VITAL vitamin D; D2d; LeBoff)

confidence_notes: Secondary DOIs: fractures 10.1056/NEJMoa2202106; diabetes 10.1056/NEJMoa1900906; synthesis 10.1016/j.jsbmb.2019.105522. Classic predictor != lever case. Grade: CONTEXT-ONLY (deficiency).

statement: Correcting genuine vitamin D deficiency (e.g. blood level under ~20 ng/mL / 50 nmol/L), with adequate calcium, supports bone health and is worthwhile; recommended maintenance/correction dose is 800-2000 IU/day, treating to a blood level rather than megadosing.
effect_size: Benefit confined to deficient/inadequate and housebound/malabsorption populations; megadosing offers no added benefit and very high doses may increase fall/fracture risk.
population: Deficient, housebound, dark-climate, or malabsorption populations

provenance.primary: Manson et al. — Principal results of VITAL and updated meta-analyses of relevant vitamin D trials, J Steroid Biochem Mol Biol 2020
provenance.surfaced_via: PubMed E-utilities (VITAL principal results / vitamin D meta)

confidence_notes: Test, don't guess. The deficiency-correction case is real; the replete-population longevity case is not. Grade: CONTEXT-ONLY.

statement: Oral magnesium supplementation (~300-400 mg/day) produces a small but real reduction in blood pressure (~2 mmHg systolic), larger in people with low magnesium status; it corrects a common dietary inadequacy.
effect_size: ~2 mmHg systolic reduction at ~300 mg/day over ~1 month in double-blind RCT meta-analysis; larger with low baseline status.
population: Adults across double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs (Zhang 2016); type-2 diabetes (Asbaghi 2021)

provenance.primary: Zhang et al. — Effects of Magnesium Supplementation on Blood Pressure: A Meta-Analysis of RCTs, Hypertension 2016

confidence_notes: Effects small and real. Glycinate/citrate preferred (oxide poorly absorbed). Sleep claims weak/low-quality. Grade: CONTEXT-ONLY.

statement: Dietary protein augments resistance-training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength, with benefit plateauing around 1.6 g/kg body weight per day in healthy training adults.
effect_size: Protein supplementation increases lean mass and strength gains during resistance training; dose-response plateaus near 1.6 g/kg/day.
population: 49 RCTs of resistance-trained and untrained adults (Morton & Phillips meta-regression)

provenance.primary: Morton, Phillips et al. — Effect of protein supplementation on resistance-training-induced gains, Br J Sports Med 2018
provenance.surfaced_via: PubMed E-utilities (protein resistance training meta Phillips)

confidence_notes: The functional-muscle optimum (~1.6 g/kg) sits far above any protein-restriction longevity prescription; the tension resolves on the age axis (mid-life caution vs elderly need). Grade: REAL.

statement: Muscle protein synthesis is switched on past a per-meal leucine threshold of roughly 2-3 g (about 20-40 g high-quality protein per meal); older and larger individuals show anabolic resistance and need a higher per-meal dose to reach the same synthetic response, partly overcome by resistance exercise.
effect_size: Per-meal leucine ~2-3 g maximizes MPS; aging blunts the response at lower doses; higher per-meal protein + exercise restores it.
population: Healthy young and older adults in MPS/amino-acid infusion and feeding studies (Shad 2016 SR; Wilkinson 2023; Layman 2015)

provenance.primary: Shad et al. — Does the MPS response to exercise and amino-acid nutrition diminish with age? A systematic review, Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab 2016; Wilkinson et al., Physiol Rep 2023; Layman et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2015
provenance.surfaced_via: PubMed E-utilities (leucine threshold muscle protein synthesis aging)

confidence_notes: Mechanism/surrogate (MPS), not a hard outcome. Distribution across 3-4 meals plausibly optimizes daily MPS; total daily intake matters most. Grade: REAL (mechanism).

statement: Higher dietary fiber intake (25-29+ g/day) is associated with 15-30% lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality and lower incidence of coronary disease, stroke, type-2 diabetes and colorectal cancer (cohort), with RCT evidence for lower LDL cholesterol, body weight and blood pressure.
effect_size: ~15-30% lower all-cause/CV mortality across cohorts; RCT-confirmed reductions in LDL, weight, BP; dose-response continues past 25-29 g/day.
population: Pooled cohorts (~135 million person-years) plus randomized trials (Reynolds & Mann Lancet series)

provenance.primary: Reynolds, Mann et al. — Carbohydrate quality and human health: a series of systematic reviews and meta-analyses, Lancet 2019

confidence_notes: Blends strong cohort mortality signal with RCT surrogate proof; among the highest-confidence dietary levers. Food-first; psyllium has its own LDL RCT support. Grade: REAL.

statement: Caffeine at 3-6 mg/kg taken ~30-60 minutes before exercise reliably improves endurance, power, sprint performance and alertness; higher doses add side effects without added performance, and tolerance develops with daily use.
effect_size: Consistent acute improvements in aerobic endurance, power and cognitive alertness at 3-6 mg/kg; no added benefit above ~9 mg/kg.
population: Healthy exercising adults across RCTs (ISSN position-stand synthesis)

provenance.primary: Guest et al. — International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: caffeine and exercise performance, J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2021

confidence_notes: Acute ergogenic, not a longevity intervention. Coffee-mortality cohort associations are observational. CYP1A2 genotype modulates response. Grade: REAL (acute performance).

statement: Collagen/gelatin peptides (~15 g with ~50 mg vitamin C) taken 30-60 minutes before loading a connective tissue increase markers of collagen synthesis, and ~2.5-15 g/day modestly improve skin elasticity/hydration; collagen does NOT build muscle and is an inferior muscle-protein source.
effect_size: Roughly doubled collagen-synthesis markers in a small tendon study; small skin-elasticity improvements in meta-analyses (many industry-funded).
population: Small RCTs of athletes/healthy adults (Shaw & Baar 2017 tendon); skin meta-analyses

provenance.primary: Shaw, Baar et al. — Vitamin C-enriched gelatin supplementation before intermittent activity augments collagen synthesis, Am J Clin Nutr 2017
provenance.surfaced_via: PubMed E-utilities (collagen gelatin vitamin C Baar)

confidence_notes: Synthesis-marker and surrogate outcomes, small/industry-influenced studies; not long-term injury outcomes. Low leucine/incomplete profile = poor for hypertrophy. Grade: CONTEXT-ONLY / EMERGING.

statement: Probiotics have real, evidence-backed benefits for specific indications (antibiotic-associated diarrhea, some IBS symptoms, certain pediatric/infectious settings) that are strain- and condition-specific; there is no evidence that a general probiotic improves healthspan, longevity, immunity or metabolic health in healthy people.
effect_size: Real for specific clinical indications (strain-specific); null/unproven for general wellness or healthspan.
population: Clinical RCT populations by indication; no healthspan endpoint in healthy adults

provenance.primary: Synthesis of strain/condition-specific probiotic meta-analyses; microbiome-aging evidence summarized in Domain C2 (_C2-SUMMARY.md)
provenance.surfaced_via: PubMed E-utilities (probiotics healthy adults systematic review) + corpus cross-ref C2

confidence_notes: Microbiome benefits in the corpus come from fermented foods/fiber, not generic capsules, and even those stop at small surrogate RCTs. Grade: CONTEXT-ONLY.

statement: NAD+ precursors (NMN, nicotinamide riboside) reliably raise blood/tissue NAD+ levels but have not produced meaningful clinical or healthspan outcomes in humans; nicotinamide riboside elevated NAD+ with no functional benefit, and NMN's strongest human signal is a single small trial of improved muscle insulin sensitivity.
effect_size: NR raises NAD+ but no change in blood pressure, arterial stiffness or metabolic outcomes; NMN one small RCT improved muscle insulin sensitivity (prediabetic women), no aging/healthspan endpoint.
population: Martens 2018: healthy middle-aged/older adults; Yoshino 2021: prediabetic postmenopausal women (small n)

provenance.primary: Martens et al. — Chronic nicotinamide riboside supplementation elevates NAD+ in healthy middle-aged and older adults, Nat Commun 2018; Yoshino et al. — NMN increases muscle insulin sensitivity in prediabetic women, Science 2021

confidence_notes: NMN secondary DOI 10.1126/science.abe9985. Raising the NAD+ biomarker != outcome (predictor != lever). Grade: HYPE.

statement: Resveratrol extends lifespan in yeast and some mouse models but human RCTs are inconsistent and largely null on meaningful clinical endpoints, compounded by poor bioavailability.
effect_size: Robust in model organisms; inconsistent/null in human trials on hard endpoints.
population: Model organisms (animal) plus mixed human RCTs

provenance.primary: Synthesis of human resveratrol RCT/meta-analysis literature (PubMed E-utilities)

confidence_notes: Classic animal-to-human translation failure; the red-wine longevity story does not survive RCTs. Grade: HYPE.

statement: High-dose antioxidant supplements (vitamin A, E, beta-carotene) do not reduce mortality in healthy people and may increase it (beta-carotene, vitamin A, vitamin E); blunting exercise-induced reactive oxygen species can also impair training adaptation.
effect_size: No mortality benefit overall; beta-carotene and vitamin A/E associated with increased mortality in the Cochrane meta-analysis.
population: ~78 RCTs, ~296,000 participants (Bjelakovic Cochrane review)

provenance.primary: Bjelakovic et al. — Antioxidant supplements for prevention of mortality in healthy participants and patients with various diseases, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2012

confidence_notes: One of the strongest 'hype can harm' results. ROS signaling is partly adaptive (hormesis, Domain H). Grade: HYPE (can harm).

statement: Multivitamin supplementation in well-nourished people produces no clear cardiovascular benefit and at most a marginal cancer and possible small cognition signal; it is largely null for hard outcomes in replete populations.
effect_size: PHS II: no CVD benefit, ~8% relative reduction in total cancer (marginal). COSMOS: small possible cognition/MCI signal, not robust.
population: PHS II ~14,600 male physicians; COSMOS older adults

provenance.primary: Sesso et al. (PHS II CVD), JAMA 2012; Gaziano et al. (PHS II cancer), JAMA 2012; Vyas et al. (COSMOS cognition), Am J Clin Nutr 2024; Sachs et al. (COSMOS MCI/dementia), Alzheimers Dement 2023

confidence_notes: Secondary DOIs: cancer 10.1001/jama.2012.14641; COSMOS cognition 10.1016/j.ajcnut.2023.12.011; COSMOS dementia 10.1002/alz.13078. Context-only if diet is genuinely poor. Grade: HYPE (context-only).

statement: Across the higher-tier evidence (PREDIMED, fiber meta-analyses, cohort data), what converges is a dietary PATTERN rather than a brand: mostly whole/minimally-processed foods, fiber-rich and plant-forward, protein-adequate, unsaturated-fat-emphasized, low in added sugar/refined starch; no diet has a hard-endpoint mortality RCT, so adherence and energy balance dominate macro tribalism.
effect_size: PREDIMED MedDiet cut major CV events ~30% (HR ~0.69) in high-risk adults; pattern components (fiber, unsaturated fat) carry their own meta-level support.
population: PREDIMED high-CV-risk adults (RCT); supporting cohorts and fiber meta-analyses

provenance.primary: Estruch et al. — PREDIMED (republished), NEJM 2018; Reynolds et al. fiber series, Lancet 2019

confidence_notes: PREDIMED carries a retraction/republication asterisk (randomization irregularities; corrected analysis still positive). No mortality-endpoint diet RCT exists. Grade: REAL (pattern), with the limits noted.

statement: Most real-world benefit of time-restricted eating is the calorie restriction it produces; calorie-matched trials show TRE no better than calorie restriction alone. The weight-independent exception is early time-restricted eating (circadian alignment), which improves insulin sensitivity and blood pressure isocalorically but is supported only by small short trials.
effect_size: Calorie-matched TRE = CR alone (Liu 2022, Trepanowski 2017); early TRE improved insulin sensitivity/BP with no weight loss but tiny n and short duration (Sutton 2018).
population: Liu 2022 n=139 12mo; Sutton 2018 n=8 prediabetic men 5 weeks; Trepanowski 2017 n=100 1yr

provenance.primary: Liu et al. — Calorie Restriction with or without TRE, NEJM 2022; Sutton/Peterson et al. — Early TRF, Cell Metab 2018

confidence_notes: Secondary DOI Sutton 10.1016/j.cmet.2018.04.010. Should-not-fast groups: disordered-eating history, underweight/frail/sarcopenic, pregnant/breastfeeding, glucose-lowering meds, heavy-training athletes. Grade: tool for CR (real); circadian timing (small real).
